'''Álvaro Mejía Pérez''' (born 18 January 1982) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played primarily as a [[central defender]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Madrid]], Mejía started his career at [[Las Rozas CF|Las Rozas]]. He signed for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 1998, subsequently moving up the various youth ranks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lasrozascf.com/2021/05/24/alvaro-zazo-y-alvaro-mejia-reciben-el-reconocimiento-de-la-familia-corazonazul/|title=Álvaro Zazo y Álvaro Mejía reciben el reconocimiento de la familia #Corazónazul|trans-title=Álvaro Zazo and Álvaro Mejía acknowledged by #Blueheart family|publisher=Las Rozas CF|first=Paula|last=Pérez-Aubá Chías|language=es|date=24 May 2021|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref>

Mejía joined the [[Real Madrid C|third team]] for [[2001–02 Tercera División|2001–02]] but moved shortly after to [[Real Madrid Castilla|the reserves]], being admitted to the main squad [[2003–04 La Liga|the following season]] and making his [[La Liga]] debut in a 2–1 home win against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] on 24 January 2004.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2004/01/25/deportes/1074985203_850215.html|title=Tyson juega en el Madrid|trans-title=Tyson plays for Madrid|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Santiago|last=Segurola|language=es|date=25 January 2004|access-date=4 January 2018}}</ref> He also appeared in the [[UEFA Champions League]]'s [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|round of 16]] on 3 March (again playing the full match) in a 1–0 home victory over [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0eaac8cb4b27-21b71e14418b-1000--mejia-circus-at-madrid/|title=Mejía circus at Madrid|publisher=UEFA|first=Adrian|last=Clarke|date=6 April 2004|access-date=11 May 2010}}</ref> In May he renewed his contract until 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0254-0d7b37413d6b-94f38cbdb3c8-1000--madrid-reward-for-mejia/|title=Madrid reward for Mejía|publisher=UEFA|date=24 May 2004|access-date=11 May 2010}}</ref> and he was subsequently put to use in different defensive positions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2868487/real-madrids-alvaro-arbeloa-has-a-special-place-in-madridismo-lore|title=Real Madrid's Alvaro Arbeloa has special place in Madridismo lore|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=10 May 2016|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref>

[[2004–05 La Liga|The following year]], Mejía appeared in just eight games for Real Madrid in all competitions, adding 26 in the league over the next two seasons. His only goal came in a 2–0 away defeat of [[Real Betis]] on 29 October 2005 after one minute on the pitch, having come on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Carlos Diogo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01ae-0ea824420704-652cc5b74517-1000--madrid-rediscover-winning-habit/|title=Madrid rediscover winning habit|publisher=UEFA|date=29 October 2005|access-date=11 May 2010}}</ref>

In July 2007, Mejía joined top-flight [[2006–07 Segunda División|newcomers]] [[Real Murcia CF|Real Murcia]] on a four-year deal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=562370.html|title=Mejía makes Murcia switch|publisher=UEFA|date=18 July 2007|access-date=1 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604211524/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=562370.html|archive-date=4 June 2016}}</ref> and scored in the first league round in a 2–1 home win over [[Real Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laverdad.es/murcia/prensa/20070826/deportes_murcia/sonrisa-para-empezar_20070826.html|title=Una sonrisa para empezar (2–1)|trans-title=A smile to start (2–1)|newspaper=[[La Verdad (Murcia)|La Verdad]]|first=César|last=García Granero|language=es|date=26 August 2007|access-date=4 January 2018}}</ref> A starter throughout the vast majority of [[2007–08 La Liga|the campaign]], he faced relegation for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2008/05/20/mas_futbol/1211234423_850215.html|title=El Murcia tiene en nómina 34 jugadores y Clemente sólo quiere 20|trans-title=Murcia have 34 players on a payroll and Clemente wants only 20|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=20 May 2008|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref>

On 30 July 2010, after Murcia [[2009–10 Segunda División|dropped another tier]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laverdad.es/murcia/20100728/deportes/real-murcia/alvaro-mejia-deja-pertenecer-201007281226.html|title=Álvaro Mejía deja de pertenecer al Real Murcia|trans-title=Álvaro Mejía is no longer a member of Real Murcia|newspaper=La Verdad|language=es|date=28 July 2010|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref> Mejía moved to [[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]] in France, [[2009–10 Ligue 2|newly promoted]] to [[Ligue 1]], on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acarlesavignon.fr/Alvaro-Perez-Mejia-Dja-Djedje-et-Kamel-Ghilas-ont-signe-_a640.html|title=Alvaro Perez Mejia, Dja Djédjé et Kamel Ghilas ont signé!|trans-title=Alvaro Perez Mejia, Dja Djédjé and Kamel Ghilas have signed!|publisher=AC Arles-Avignon|language=fr|date=30 July 2010|access-date=5 August 2010}}</ref> In January of the following year, he changed teams – and countries – again, signing for Turkish [[Süper Lig]] club [[Konyaspor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mercato365.com/etranger/monde/article_487673_Arles-Avignon-Mejia-a-Konyaspor-.shtml|title=Mejia à Konyaspor|trans-title=Mejia at Konyaspor|publisher=Mercato 365|language=fr|date=15 January 2011|access-date=16 January 2011}}</ref>

On 13 July 2012, Mejía agreed to a one-year deal with [[UD Almería|Almería]] in the [[Segunda División]], after passing his medical.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://udalmeria.ideal.es/noticias/2012-07-13/almeria-ficha-alvaro-mejia-201207131409.html|title=El Almería ficha a Álvaro Mejia|trans-title=Almería sign Álvaro Mejia|newspaper=[[Ideal (newspaper)|Ideal]]|first=Juanjo|last=Aguilera|language=es|date=13 July 2012|access-date=4 January 2018}}</ref> On 18 June 2014, after [[2013–14 Super League Greece|one season]] in the [[Super League Greece]] with [[Ergotelis F.C.|Ergotelis]], he joined newly promoted [[Qatar Stars League]] side [[Al Shahaniya SC|Al Shahaniya]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qsl.com.qa/users/newsen/NewsDetails.aspx?pid=2219|title=Al Shahaniya signs contract with Spaniard Alvaro Perez|publisher=[[Qatar Stars League]]|date=19 June 2014|access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref>
